purpose: Category-level research for the physical AI stack beyond GPUs: networking, optics, memory/HBM packaging, power/grid, funded interconnection, microgrids/time-to-power, reliability, cooling, water and industrial automation. Research-only; no site/UI/scoring architecture changes.
categoryRead: The physical-AI thesis remains strong but increasingly bifurcates into three evidence tiers: funded utility interconnections, behind-the-meter/microgrid time-to-power, and speculative headline load requests. Vertiv's Sep 2 agreement to acquire UtilityInnovation Group is the freshest validation that onsite generation orchestration, microgrid controls and specialised switchgear are becoming a strategic data-centre category. At the same time, >700 GW of US grid requests still requires deposit/funding screens. August ISM remains constructive for real equipment demand: Production 58.3, Prices 71.1 and persistent electrical/electronic, memory, semiconductor, copper and wire scarcity.

newRiskLens.name: Funded load quality / ghost demand
newRiskLens.evidence: US data-centre grid requests exceed 700 GW; Texas and several utilities are screening ownership, funding, deposits and duplicate requests.
newRiskLens.implication: Supplier order books backed by real customers become more valuable than utility load forecasts or developer announcements. Utilities/developers that overstate future load face capex, ratepayer and valuation risk.
newRiskLens.confirmation: Verified/deposit-backed MW remains strong while speculative requests are cancelled and supplier booked orders hold.
newRiskLens.invalidation: Audits show most requests are fully funded and committed, leaving headline queue totals broadly intact.
newRiskLens.nextTest: Texas/PJM/AEP/Exelon audit/deposit data and named hyperscaler interconnection milestones.

newOpportunityLens.name: Time-to-power / data-centre microgrids
newOpportunityLens.evidence: Vertiv agreed to acquire UtilityInnovation Group for ~$1.45B cash plus up to $1.15B contingent consideration. UIG adds microgrid controls, microgrid-specific switchgear and behind-the-meter power architecture to Vertiv's existing grid-to-chip platform.
newOpportunityLens.implication: Onsite generation and control can bridge slow utility interconnections, making microgrid architecture a monetising layer rather than merely a contingency plan. It also creates a second route to validate data-centre demand: actual equipment/control orders rather than requested MW.
newOpportunityLens.confirmation: Hyperscalers disclose more customer-funded onsite generation/microgrid deployments and VRT/UIG backlog/order conversion accelerates.
newOpportunityLens.invalidation: Utility interconnection times compress materially or customers reject onsite-generation economics.
newOpportunityLens.nextTest: VRT deal close/integration guidance, microgrid customer wins, and competitor orders.

VRT.read: UIG materially broadens the addressable stack from power/cooling into microgrid controls, specialised switchgear and onsite-generation orchestration. Strategic fit improved enough for a 7.3→7.7 research upgrade; premium valuation and integration cost still cap conviction.

BDC.read: Record Q2 orders remain stronger evidence than demand forecasts. Keep focus on book-to-bill and named data-centre/industrial wins.

GNRC.read: Roughly $1.6bn data-centre backlog remains useful because it is booked demand; microgrid expansion increases the strategic value of controllable onsite generation, but customer/project quality and backlog conversion remain the tests.

AMKR.read: NVIDIA demand and customer prepayments support utilisation/financing quality; heavy capex and FCF conversion remain constraints.

0522.HK.role: HBM TCB/hybrid bonding + photonics + AI-server SMT
0522.HK.read: HBM/advanced-packaging equipment demand remains supported by component scarcity; qualification/order conversion and valuation are the next tests.

SLB.read: Kelvion remains a differentiated thermal-management entry; require integration, customer quality and 2028 target execution before further promotion.

AGKO.read: High-priority IPO watch because time-to-power can bypass grid queues. VRT/UIG independently validates the category, but customer contracts, IPO leverage and valuation remain mandatory checks.

existingCoreCrossRead.GEV: Generation/grid demand remains high quality when orders are named/contracted; microgrid/on-site generation can expand the addressable reliability stack but aggregate interconnection queues remain insufficient evidence by themselves.
existingCoreCrossRead.ETN: Switchgear/power-management shortages remain confirmed by ISM; microgrids add another demand path for distribution/control equipment. High real yields remain a multiple headwind.
existingCoreCrossRead.PWR: Transmission/substations remain essential for verified large-load interconnections, while microgrids are complementary rather than substitutes for long-term grid buildout.
existingCoreCrossRead.POWL: Order/backlog evidence remains strong; valuation/execution constrain entry quality.
existingCoreCrossRead.VRT: UIG turns time-to-power into a more complete grid-to-chip offering. Upgrade research conviction to 7.7, but require deal close, integration and customer-funded order proof before another move.
existingCoreCrossRead.FLEX: Planned Cloud & Power Infrastructure spin is strategically aligned; apply both funded-load and customer-concentration tests to backlog/guidance.
existingCoreCrossRead.YTLPOWR: Strategic power/data-centre exposure remains strong. VRT/UIG validates the global bottleneck but does not substitute for YTLPOWR-specific contracted utilisation, leverage and cash conversion.
existingCoreCrossRead.ROK: Profitable factory/warehouse automation remains the preferred first-wave robotics/physical-AI expression.

augustISMPhysicalStack.signal: Physical activity is still expanding, but orders/backlog slowed while input inflation and delivery stress stayed severe. Electrical/electronic components, memory, semiconductors, copper and wire remain direct bottleneck evidence.

roboticsRead: No adoption-wave change: warehouse/fixed industrial automation first, cobots/mobile manipulation second, industrial humanoids third, open-world/general-purpose robots last. TSLA's Cybercab event is an autonomy catalyst, not evidence that industrial humanoids have leapfrogged fixed automation economics.
nextTests: VRT/UIG close, integration guidance and microgrid wins
Texas/PJM/AEP/Exelon data-centre load audits and deposits
PWR/ETN/GEV/FLEX named orders and backlog conversion
